info.name: Server Rules & University Record
info.description:
Every endpoint of both services, through the Gateway, as a client and as a service reach them now.

It used to run against the two services standing alone on ports 8001 and 8002, with access control faked by made-up bearer strings. Neither port is published any more and neither service decides who may read what: a session token does, and the Gateway hands the identity over. The first folder therefore opens a real shift and issues a real token per record slice — enrollment, emails, courses, schedule, fcim, and one holding none — plus a second shift, for the reads that must be refused because they come from elsewhere.

What each request asks is unchanged. What changed is the door it arrives at and who it says it is, and in a few places the answer: an endpoint the contract marks internal is refused on the published port with 403 INTERNAL_ENDPOINT before the token is even read, and a record read names its own shape rather than a hand-made applicant's values.

`POST /rules`, `POST /rules/evaluate` and `POST /applicants` go to gateway:8001, which is not published, so the collection runs from inside the Docker network:

    docker run --rm --network pad-team-20_backend -v "$PWD/postman:/etc/newman" \
      postman/newman run server-rules-and-university-record.postman_collection.json \
      --env-var gatewayBaseUrl=http://gateway:8000

Each run creates its own players, team and shift, so it can be run repeatedly without resetting anything.

item.name: 0. Real sessions and real tokens
item.description:
The access control these two services apply is carried entirely in the session token: its `sessionId` and its `recordAccess`. This folder produces one real token per record slice by assigning the junior a slice and issuing a token, seven times over, before the shift starts — and a second shift for the other-session token.

`POST /rules`, `POST /rules/evaluate` and `POST /applicants` are marked internal in the contract: a service calls them and a client may not. They go to `gateway:8001`, which is not published, so the collection runs from inside the Docker network:

    docker run --rm --network pad-team-20_backend -v "$PWD/postman:/etc/newman" \
      postman/newman run server-rules-and-university-record.postman_collection.json \
      --env-var gatewayBaseUrl=http://gateway:8000

item.name: Server Rules Service
item.description: Run the entire collection in order against the local lab implementation. Creates three rule versions per run; no cleanup endpoint exists. Captures generated versions automatically; never assumes version 1. Uses public mock tokens, not real JWTs. Tests config/rules.php provisional policy. Requires the Server Rules endpoint feature branch. Change rulesBaseUrl if the service port changes. Do not define environment variables matching generated collection IDs. Negative tests are expected to pass on the specified error status. No Docker/PostgreSQL or shared-stack integration is claimed.

item.name: University Record Service
item.description: Run the entire collection in order against the local lab implementation. POST /applicants consumes the repeatable mocked ApplicantInitialized story; it is not a real story-generator call. Captures applicantId automatically. Replays do not replace stored ground truth. Uses public mock session tokens and the fixed reference data documented in the service README. No Session call, real JWT validation, RabbitMQ or shared-stack integration is assumed. Change recordsBaseUrl if necessary. Do not create environment variables shadowing generated collection IDs. Academic-year needs authentication but never an assignment. Error requests count as passing tests when their expected status/envelope matches.

// The README's contract gives this enum as

// 'banned'. Asserted here as the system behaves; which of the two
// is wrong is University Record's owner to say.
